From white rapids rise a pair of horns as a silvette races upstream following the scent of blood still fresh in the rushing waters. Th ese 
scavengers, armored in plates of overlapping scales reminiscent of a fi sh from a bygone era, battle with larkiera and nicalliath for recent 
kills. To contend with such competition, razored protrusions along their face and hardened scales protect them while they wrestle 
for hunks of meat. Lacking the patience of an ambush predator, these fi sh instead migrate great distances, attacking every fi sh and 
amphibian they can smell, with in an unshaken faith in the protection of their armored scales. While this aggressive behavior has seen 
this species spread through much of the Fenlands, many larger predators have taken advantage of the mindless brute.
Class - Actinopterygii • Genus Derived Evolution - Ctenolucius • Niche - Aquatic Carnivore Scavenger 
Preyed upon by - Nicalliath, Nuthorghull • Preys on - Larkiera, Murrow, Parro, Rauka, Varrip

Multiattack Th e silvette makes two attacks with its Curved

Curved Toothed Bite Melee Attack Roll: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one

Razored Scales Melee Attack Roll: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one

takes an extra 9 (2d8) Slashing damage. Strength Saving Th row:

Aggressive Instinct (1/Day) Always ready to move, the silvette responds 
quickly when hit.
Reaction - Trigger: When the silvette is hit with a ranged attack 
Response - Wisdom Saving Th row: DC 10, the silvette. Success: It 
moves towards the attacking creature and makes a Razored Scale 
Melee attack roll. Th is Reaction doesn’t provoke an Opportunity 
Attack when the silvette swims out of an enemy’s reach.

Encountering As solitary scavengers with miles of rivers to 
roam, spilled blood is the best method to catch this fi sh. Silvette 
are often the fi rst to arrive, their streamlined bodies cutting 
through the water quickly as they expertly track the scent. 
Th ough it is never long before the water erupts with competing 
scavengers and a Traveler would be wise to capture the silvette 
before the slower scavengers arrive.
Rows of backward facing teeth clamp 
onto chunks of flesh, allowing the fish to 
escape without losing its hard-won meal
A multitude of nares run down 
the fish’s snout, leading to highly 
sensitive olfactory receptors to detect 
blood in the water from miles away
Hardened plates of razor edged scales 
rise in horn-like protrusions along 
its body, capable of inflicting terrible 
harm with strikes from the fish’s head 
Silvette eggs latch on tightly to streamweed, 
camouflaged as they move along in the 
river current, staying oxidized and safe in 
the sanctuary of the long waxy leaves that 
spread across the river floor
